[PER :- SHYAM C. CHANDAK, J.] :-
1)

Petitioners accused in F.I.R. bearing No.7/2016 registered with Deccan Police Station, Pune for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 464, 467, 468, 471,
read with 34 of the Indian Penal Code, have preferred this Petition for quashing of the said F.I.R. by consent of Respondent No.2, on the ground that, the matter has been settled between the Petitioners and Respondent No.2 through its Authorized Manager.

2) Record indicates that, by an Order dated 27 th November 2017, notice was issued to Respondent No.2 and ad-interim relief was granted in terms of prayer clause (b) qua the Petitioners, till the next date.
Thereafter, Advocate Mr. Rajesh Khobragade appeared for the Respondent No.2.
3) The said F.I.R. No.7/2016 came to be registered on the report of Shantaram V. Shenoy, Manager of Respondent No.2.

The F.I.R. alleges that, accused Abhishek More and Mrs. Bina More had purchased a tenement bearing No.1104, 11th Floor, Gulmohar Building, Green Vally Co- operative Housing Society, Wanwadi, Pune on 5 th March, 2004.

entities.text: Green Vally Co- operative Housing Society, Wanwadi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Later on, the More couple sold the above referred flat to the Petitioners on 27 th September, 2012.
Further, on 24 th April, 2015 Petitioner Ashish Shah sold Jyoti WP-2441-2017 final.doc the said flat to co-accused Irfan Sattar Shaikh and Ms.Sajia Irfan Sattar Shaikh.

At that time the Shaikh couple had obtained a loan of Rs.1.5 Crores Sunita Pankaj Shah And Ors vs The State Of Maharashtra And Anr on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140462139/
2 from Respondent No.2, to purchase the said flat.

entities.text: Crores Sunita Pankaj Shah And Ors vs The State Of Maharashtra And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, accused Irfan Shaikh defaulted in payment of the loan installments, which forced the Respondent No.2 to initiate a legal action.

During said action Respondent No.2 learnt that, the Petitioners had already availed a loan from Capital First Company by registered mortgage of the said flat on 19 th August, 2013 and the 'N.O.C.'
of the Green Valley Co-operative Society submitted with the Respondent No.2, was bogus.

Thus, the Petitioners concealing the fact of previous loan and the registered mortgage, obtained a huge loan amount of Rs.1.5 Crores from Respondent No.2 by pretending that, they have sold the said flat to the accused Shaikh Couple.
Thus, the Petitioners and their co- accused committed this crime.
4) Heard learned counsel Mr. Katariya for the Petitioners, learned APP Ms. A. A. Takalkar for the Respondent No.1-State and learned counsel Mr. Khobragade for Respondent No.2.
Perused the record.

5) Learned counsel for the Petitioners submitted that, during the pendency of the investigation itself, the Petitioners and Respondent No.2 have settled this matter and accordingly, Petitioners have refunded the entire loan of Rs.1.5 Crores to the Respondent No.2.
Therefore, the Respondent No.2 has no objection for quashing of the F.I.R. in part i.e., qua Jyoti WP-2441-2017 final.doc the Petitioners.
Quashing F.I.R. in such a manner is permissible in law.
Hence, the Petition may be considered accordingly and the F.I.R. may be quashed qua the Petitioners.

To support his submission, the learned Advocate relied on following decisions:
i) Lovely Salhotra and Another Vs. State (NCT OF Delhi) and Another reported in (2018) 12 Supreme Court Cases 391.
ii) Jayrajsinh Digvijasinh Rana Vs. State of Gujarat and Another reported in (2012)
12 Supreme Court Cases, 401.
iii) Alpesh Arvindbhai Patel & Ors. Vs. The State of Maharashtra & Anr.
vide Order dated 17th March 2023 in Cr. Writ Petition No.3721/2018.
6)

sentences.text: Per contra learned APP submitted that, the investigation in the present crime is completed and the charge-sheet is ready to be filed.
There is sufficient material against the Petitioners and other co-accused showing their involvement in the said crime.
Hence necessary Orders may be passed in the interest of justice.

7) Considering the Petition and the submissions, this Court informed the learned Advocate for the Petitioners that, in view of the settled position of law, quashing of the F.I.R. in part i.e., in respect of some of the accused is not permissible.

Therefore, the learned Advocate was suggested to argue the matter on merits, however, he bluntly refused it by raising a specious plea that he has no instructions to do it and stated that, the Petition may be decided in the light of the decisions cited above.
In the backdrop, we have carefully considered the said decisions.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In so far as the decision in the case of Lovely Salhotra (supra) is concerned, in the said case the Hon'ble Supreme Court allowed the quashing of the F.I.R. in part because no offence was made out against the co-accused Nos. 2, 3, 4 and 6 also.

The said F.I.R. filed against the Appellants by Respondent No.2 therein, was afterthought and intended to pressurize the Appellants not to prosecute the criminal complaint filed by them under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act.
In the said case the Hon'ble Supreme Court has taken into consideration entire evidence on record.
As against this, in the case in hand there is a strong prima facie case against the Petitioners and co-accused of having committed the offences alleged in the said F.I.R..

9) In the cited case of Jayarajsinh Rana (supra), the F.I.R. under Sections 467, 468, 471, 420 and 120-B of the I.P.C. was registered against the Appellant/accused No.3 on allegations that, Accused No.1 and 2 sold certain plots of the first informant/Respondent No.2 to the Appellant with the help of bogus documents.
Thereafter, the matter was settled between the Appellant and Respondent No.2.

As per the terms of settlement, the Appellant executed an Affidavit stating that, he will withdraw the Civil Suit filed by him for specific performance and declaration by accepting that he has not any legal right, title and claim over the various plots in issue, as they were sold to him by the main accused No.1 and 2 on the basis of Jyoti WP-2441-2017 final.doc forged documents.

Further,
the Appellant assured the Respondent No.2 that he will not claim any right, title and interest over the various plots belonging to the Respondent No.2.

The Appellant also demonstrated that in fact,
he was a victim of the crime as he was cheated by the main accused Nos.1 and 2, therefore, he has filed a separate F.I.R. against them.

In this background the Hon'ble Supreme Court quashed and set aside the F.I.R. qua the Appellant/Accused No.3 only but invoking its powers under Article 142 of the Constitution of India to do the complete justice.
Thus, the facts of this reported case are materially distinct from the facts of the case in hand.

10) In the case of Alpesh Patel (supra), in view of the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case that, the settlement was arrived at between the parties in the concerned Civil Suit and the proceedings before MahaRERA, the Division Bench of this Court quashed the subject F.I.R. in part i.e., qua 7 out of total 9 accused and allowed the Investigation Officer to proceed with the investigation against the said two accused in the manner as the law mandates.
11) According to us F.I.R. or charge-sheet cannot be quashed in part qua a few or selected accused even with the consent of the victim/informant.
An accused having financial and/or muscle power may cause/pressurise the victim/informant for amicable settlement, leaving the co-accused to face trial, who is/are lacking the said factors.
Therefore, the Jyoti WP-2441-2017 final.doc F.I.R. in part even with consent of victim cannot be quashed.
The F.I.R. can be quashed in entirety against all accused with consent of victim.
It can be quashed in part, only on merits and not otherwise.

12) Thus, even though the F.I.R. in question is not fit to be quashed in part i.e., to the extent of Petitioners even with the consent, learned Advocate for the Petitioners kept insisting on this Court to adopt it as a practice and as a matter of course.
This insistence was continued even after he bluntly refused to argue the Petition on merit when we requested and then orally directed for the same in view of the settled position of law.

We do not appreciate such a practice as this way, the learned Advocate exhibited scant respect towards the oral directions issued by this Court initially in Sunita Pankaj Shah And Ors vs The State Of Maharashtra And Anr on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140462139/
4 the form of request to him and subsequently in the form of oral Orders.

sentences.text:
There can be more to express about the conduct of the learned Advocate for the Petitioners, however, except expressing that we felt extremely sorry about the said act, we do not think it proper to add anything more to that.
12.1) The Petition accordingly fails and stands dismissed.

(SHYAM C. CHANDAK, J.) (A. S. GADKARI, J.)
